problem.title: Telehealth Providers Above Regional Average Completion Rate
problem.prompt: A telehealth platform tracks appointment outcomes by provider. Each appointment record belongs to one provider and includes whether the visit was completed (the provider signed off). Management wants to identify providers whose completion rate exceeds their region's average. Write a query that computes each provider's completion rate (completed visits / total visits) and their region's average completion rate, then returns only providers whose personal rate is strictly above their region's average. Output columns: `provider_id`, `provider_name`, `region`, `completion_rate` (rounded to 4 decimals), `region_avg_rate` (rounded to 4 decimals). Order by `region` ASC, then `completion_rate` DESC. If a provider has zero visits, exclude them. Handle the case where a region might have providers with identical rates.

composite_moves: group by provider to compute completion_rate
window function AVG(completion_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY region) to get region_avg_rate
filter WHERE completion_rate > region_avg_rate in outer query
order by region ASC, completion_rate DESC

hints: You'll need to compute each provider's completion rate first, then compare it to their region's average.
Use a CTE to calculate completion rates by provider, then a window function AVG(...) OVER (PARTITION BY region) with no ORDER BY to attach the region average to every row.
In the outer query, filter WHERE completion_rate > region_avg_rate. Remember to join providers to get region and name, and round both rates to 4 decimals.
problem.answer_key: WITH provider_rates AS (SELECT p.provider_id, p.provider_name, p.region, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN a.completed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::NUMERIC / COUNT(*)::NUMERIC, 4) AS completion_rate FROM providers p JOIN appointments a ON p.provider_id = a.provider_id GROUP BY p.provider_id, p.provider_name, p.region), rates_with_avg AS (SELECT provider_id, provider_name, region, completion_rate, ROUND(AVG(completion_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY region), 4) AS region_avg_rate FROM provider_rates) SELECT provider_id, provider_name, region, completion_rate, region_avg_rate FROM rates_with_avg WHERE completion_rate > region_avg_rate ORDER BY region ASC, completion_rate DESC;

_meta.scenario: a telehealth visit completion funnel from booking to provider sign-off

user_solution:
/*
Write a query that computes each provider's completion rate (completed visits / total visits) and their region's average completion rate, then returns only providers whose personal rate is strictly above their region's average.

1. group appointments
2. region average
3. join

*/
WITH base AS (
SELECT
        p.provider_id,
        p.provider_name,
        p.region,
        ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN a.completed = true THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),4) AS completion_rate
    FROM appointments AS a
    JOIN providers AS p
        ON a.provider_id = p.provider_id
    GROUP BY p.provider_id
),
cal_region AS (
SELECT 
    *,
    ROUND(AVG(completion_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY region
                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING), 4) AS region_avg_rate
FROM base
)
SELECT *
FROM cal_region
WHERE completion_rate > region_avg_rate
ORDER BY region, completion_rate DESC
;
